harness_evolution.correction: Uniform task lifecycle/echo-buffer management correction removes the evolved benchmark harness's excess TCP brk/minor-fault/kernel-CPU activity; this is not a multiplexer runtime algorithm improvement
harness_evolution.raw_sampled_profiles: excluded; CPU attribution samples are not wall-time measurements

measurement_notes: Hyperfine warmup1/runs3 per block; W/R macro uses two interleaved ABBA blocks, giving12 measured process runs per variant per transport
Sizing cells use3 measured process runs; noisy TCP cells retain standard deviations and direct observations in original artifacts
All recorded macro cells validate exactly4GiB request-plus-echo payload and2048 exchanges
Direct latency guardrails use20 processes per condition across10 paired blocks; quantiles are per-process nearest-rank exchange quantiles, not pooled service latency
Mixed workloads are closed-loop fixed concurrency (1bulk+7small), not fixed arrival rate; actual request/byte counts are retained separately by class
Hyperfine includes process startup/setup/warmup; CLI elapsed excludes setup and warmup; perf counter executions are separate and include timeout wrapper/startup/setup/warmup
No strict p99 noninferiority bound is established from noisy intervals; report observed stable harm and uncertainty under the predeclared5percent budget
No allocator environment, CPU affinity or sysctl changes were made

measurement_recommendations.bounded_reader: supported by replicated bulk improvements and recvfrom reduction; final small/mixed interactive controls show no stable greater-than5percent p99 harm, with disclosed uncertainty
measurement_recommendations.full_prefix_and_refill: reject: legacy-harness TCP slower despite fewer writes; combined slower than lookahead alone
measurement_recommendations.larger_defaults: reject: all larger native matched diagonals are slower, and128KiB has stable greater-than5percent p99 harm in single TCP, small duplex and single duplex controls

mismatch_controls.reason: 16KiB is the native bulk winner on both transports; 128KiB is the best larger stock-engine diagonal candidate, selected for caller-versus-DATA attribution and adverse-tail controls, not as a native winner

previous_capture_comparison.interpretation: The previous capture used an inline fixed-size echo scratch and different harness lifetimes. The new capture uses dynamically sized buffers and the corrected uniform lifecycle. These cross-capture changes are not isolated runtime gains; use the fresh same-harness W/R comparison for the reader effect. No speedup ratios are chained.
